reason: Conversation 1 repeated an identical boilerplate safety block and never engaged with the homeowner's direct question about the fuse box, the spreading water, or the still-running machine, and its blanket 'engineer must check the machine' advice was never refined. Conversation 2 gave the same initial safety guidance but then answered 'yes, turn it off' with correct constraints (don't reach plugs/extension lead, only go to the consumer unit if reachable without the water), recognised the suds as a washing-up-liquid overflow rather than a seal failure, confirmed it with one sensible question, and when the homeowner said they couldn't safely reach the fuse box it correctly told them to leave the area and get help/999 if sparking, plus involve the landlord. Conversation 2's only weakness is slightly over-escalating by insisting the dishwasher itself needs an engineer before reuse, but it did avoid any part recommendation, so it clearly served the homeowner better.
